official.description_text:
Postdoc in Generative AI for humanoid assistive robots
Login and apply
KTH Royal Institute of Technology, School of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science
Job description
We are seeking a postdoctoral researcher with an interest in generative AI, machine learning, natural language processing, and human–robot interaction. You will work within a newly awarded project at the
Department of Speech, Music and Hearing
at the School of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science (EECS) at KTH. TMH is an internationally recognized research environment in speech and language technology, with a particular focus on multimodal interaction with social robots. The newly launched Promobilia-funded project
SAInt
: Situated Agentic Interaction aims to develop and evaluate humanoid assistive robots capable of understanding context, learning through interaction, and providing proactive support. The goal is to contribute to reducing the care gap for older adults and people with special needs. Within the five-year project, the doctoral student will collaborate with researchers and doctoral students at the
Department of Robotics, Perception and Learning
. The overall objective of SAInt is to move beyond traditional robotics for support and assistance, which rely on explicit command structures, and instead develop agentic systems capable of contextual understanding, inferring user goals through natural multimodal communication, and collaborating proactively as an integrated part of everyday activities. Your task is to develop and evaluate a dialogue architecture that moves beyond reactive systems and enables the humanoid robot to understand user goals, actions, ongoing activities, and cognitive states, in order to determine when and how verbal and physical assistance should be provided.
Qualifications
Requirements
A doctoral degree or an equivalent foreign degree in computer science, machine learning, computational linguistics, robotics, human–computer interaction, or a closely related field. This eligibility requirement must be met no later than the time the employment decision is made.
Documented experience in experimentally evaluating robots that interact through speech.
Strong programming skills (e.g., Python, PyTorch).
Ability to work both independently and collaboratively within an interdisciplinary team.
Preferred qualifications
A doctoral degree or an equivalent foreign degree, obtained within the last three years prior to the application deadline
Previous experience in developing and evaluating robots that interact through speech training is highly meritorious. Great emphasis will be placed on personal skills.
Awareness of diversity and equal opportunity issues, with specific focus on gender equality
Great emphasis will be placed on personal skills.
Join us at KTH
KTH shapes the future through education, research and innovation. As a leading international technical university, we play an active role in advancing the transition towards a sustainable society. At KTH, you have the opportunity to grow and develop in a creative and dynamic environment, with good working conditions and attractive benefits. Equality, diversity and equal opportunities are essential to quality and form an integral part of KTH’s core values as a university and public authority.
Learn more about our benefits and what it's like to work and grow at KTH.

Log into KTH's recruitment system to apply for this position. You are responsible for ensuring that your application is complete according to the instructions in the ad.
The application must include:

Copy of diplomas and grades from your previous university studies. Translations into English or Swedish if the original documents have not been issued in any of these languages.
Brief account of why you want to conduct research, your academic interests and how they relate to your previous studies and future goals. Maximally two pages long.
Your complete application must be received at KTH no later than the last day of application, midnight CET/CEST (Central European Time/Central European Summer Time).

ai.summary: Postdoctoral position at KTH Department of Speech, Music and Hearing developing dialogue architectures and multimodal interaction systems for humanoid assistive robots. Focus is on generative AI, natural language processing, context understanding, and speech-based human–robot interaction for older adults and people with special needs.

thematic_fit.rationale: Partial thematic overlap on social interaction and human-centred design, but core position is ML/NLP-driven robotics, not immersive systems or spatial learning. Position targets dialogue and assistive robotics; candidate's research is spatial cognition, wayfinding, and collaborative XR. Shared ground: multimodal user interaction, understanding user needs/context, collaborative systems design. Divergence: SAInt is fundamentally a generative AI + robotics project; candidate's strength is XR application design and user-centred evaluation, not dialogue systems or large language models.

methodological_fit.rationale: Moderate methodological overlap. Both involve human–computer interaction evaluation (candidate: user studies, tech acceptance; position: robot interaction evaluation). Candidate has intermediate user-studies and experimental-design skills applicable to robot interaction experiments. However, position core is generative AI / NLP / PyTorch development—candidate is advanced in Unity/C# and beginner in Python, with no documented ML/NLP experience. Dialogue architecture development requires machine learning competency; candidate's quantitative research is user-study focused, not model training. Multimodal interaction (speech + context understanding) is present in both, but at different levels: candidate's multiplayer collaboration is game-based; position's multimodal is speech-centric with LLM backends.

growth_value.rationale: Moderate growth value, but with risk. Position would deepen candidate's understanding of social robot interaction, multimodal user understanding, and context-aware systems—valuable for understanding how immersive systems could support assistive tasks. However, learning Python/PyTorch and generative AI from scratch during a postdoc is ambitious and may compete with consolidating XR research trajectory. Growth in HCI evaluation methods and assistive technology design is genuine; growth in ML/NLP would be high-effort catch-up rather than deepening existing strengths. Does not close core capability gaps (spatial cognition research, VR evaluation methodologies).

strategic_value.rationale: Strong institutional fit: KTH is highly ranked; Department of Speech, Music and Hearing is internationally recognized in multimodal interaction. Stockholm is in preferred geography (Sweden). Promobilia funding indicates stable multi-year project (5 years) with clear research vision. Collaboration with Department of Robotics, Perception and Learning adds interdisciplinary credibility. Position offers first postdoc opportunity and publication pathway. However, strategic misalignment: position is positioned as a bridge away from XR/immersive systems toward ML-driven assistive robotics. KTH EECS is strong but not known as an immersive systems hub; supervisory expertise (speech/dialogue, robotics) does not build candidate's target HCI/XR identity. Would be a strong postdoc strategically if aligned with candidate's goals, but represents a methodological pivot.

eligibility_flags: Position requires PhD obtained no later than time of employment decision. Candidate's MSc is in-progress (thesis stage); PhD eligibility is not met. Candidate must complete and defend MSc before eligibility threshold.
Strong programming skills in Python required; candidate has beginner-level Python with no substantial project experience. PyTorch use is expected but not documented in candidate profile.

Documented experience experimentally evaluating robots that interact through speech is preferred and meritorious. Candidate has no robot or speech interaction evaluation background, only XR-based user studies.
Position emphasizes recent PhD (within 3 years) and speech-interaction development/evaluation experience as preferred qualifications. Candidate meets neither.
risks: Significant competency gap in core deliverables: developing dialogue architecture requires NLP/generative AI expertise candidate does not have. Learning curve during postdoc is steep.
Python/PyTorch skill gap is non-trivial. Candidate is advanced in C#/Unity, but postdoc positions typically assume language fluency at start.

Thematic mismatch: position targets assistive robotics with dialogue; candidate's identity is immersive learning and spatial cognition. Completing this postdoc would signal a career pivot toward HRI and away from XR.
Supervisory expertise (speech technology, robotics) does not overlap with target HCI/XR mentorship needs.
Candidate likely ineligible at time of application (MSc incomplete); would need to defer or reapply post-graduation.
Department of Speech, Music and Hearing is not known for immersive systems or VR research; limited institutional resources for candidate's target research direction post-postdoc.
